papers.title: Diurnal variations of psychometric indicators in Twitter content

source_blocks.text: The study examined temporal changes in psychometric indicators derived from word lists in Twitter content.
The authors sampled English-language tweets from the United Kingdom every hour for four years.
Two independent factors explained 85% of the observed variation in the psychometric indicators.

papers.title: Playing Super Mario 64 increases hippocampal grey matter in older adults

source_blocks.text: Healthy adults aged 55 to 75 years were randomly assigned to video-game training, music lessons, or a no-contact control condition.
The six-month intervention included 8 participants in the video-game group, 12 in music, and 13 in the control group.
Hippocampal grey-matter increases were observed only in the video-game training group.

papers.title: The shape of a glass influences alcoholic beverage consumption

source_blocks.text: The experiment tested whether glass shape affected drinking rate for alcoholic and non-alcoholic beverages.
A total of 159 social alcohol drinkers were randomly assigned to receive a beverage in a straight or curved glass.
For a full alcoholic beverage, drinking time was about 60% slower from a straight glass than from a curved glass; this difference was not observed for the non-alcoholic beverage.

papers.title: Social relationships and mortality risk: a meta-analytic review

source_blocks.text: The meta-analysis examined the relationship between social relationships and mortality risk.
The review included 148 studies with 308,849 participants.
Across studies, stronger social relationships were associated with a 50% greater likelihood of survival (odds ratio 1.50); estimates varied by how social relationships were measured.

papers.title: Association between excessive internet use and sleep disturbance

source_blocks.text: The cross-sectional study examined internet use and sleep disturbance among Japanese adolescents.
Questionnaire data were analyzed from 57,425 junior and senior high-school students.

Compared with less than one hour of daily internet use, adjusted odds ratios for sleep disturbance were 1.23, 1.42, and 1.56 for successively higher use categories; the cross-sectional design cannot establish causality.

papers.title: Battle for the thermostat: Gender and the effect of temperature on cognitive performance

source_blocks.text: The laboratory experiment investigated how ambient temperature affected cognitive performance for men and women.

papers.title: Pre-infection 25-hydroxyvitamin D3 levels and association with severity of COVID-19 illness

source_blocks.text: The retrospective study examined whether pre-infection vitamin D levels were associated with COVID-19 disease severity.
Among 1,176 admitted patients, 253 had a vitamin D measurement from 14 to 730 days before a positive PCR test.

Vitamin D deficiency was observed in 87.4% of patients with severe or critical disease and 34.3% of patients with mild or moderate disease; the adjusted odds ratio was 14 with a 95% confidence interval from 4 to 51.
